recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5241; future extension-handling changes should preserve the later FHIR-18362 preserve-if-possible rule.
issue_request: FHIR-5241 was Published/Persuasive for Jan 2015 Ballot Comment #118 against FHIR-core extensibility. It asked to clarify the confusing sentence "When reading elements, ignore other extensions, unless you want to read a particular extension" with guidance to read and process understood extensions and ignore others.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite SVN revision 4505. Git commit ce8baad35f1728a0a523750f0784acec1d15efc1 is the git-svn import of that revision and changed source/extensibility.html to "When reading elements, read and process the extensions you know and use, and ignore other extensions."
additional_context: The current source has a later same-bullet refinement from FHIR-18362, already represented on the combined branch, requiring preservation of unrecognized non-modifier extensions when possible and special handling for unrecognized modifier extensions. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-5241 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change was made because the current source already satisfies FHIR-5241 and rolling back to the older literal ignore wording would conflict with FHIR-18362.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue refined the same Summary bullet, so it governs the current wording after the FHIR-5241 clarification.

evidence_items.learned: The active current source conveys the FHIR-5241 clarification and no longer contains the original confusing sentence.
